text: After weaning, sows should return to oestrus as soon as possible (ideally 5–10 days, if in good body condition) to avoid feeding non-productive sows; stress and light both matter for this. The mating area should be bright, with a light left on until 10 pm as an advantage, and the sow should not be kept in a quiet space — she needs some stress/excitation, such as a nearby boar or noise, to help bring on oestrus. Pregnant sows need calm surroundings and should not fight with other sows — individual cages are recommended. Floor quality is crucial: 90% of lameness in pregnant sows, the most important disorder in this group, is due to poor floor condition, and lameness that makes standing and moving difficult leads to sows eating and drinking too little.
